On August 21, 2026, Megan Holdings Limited shareholders approved a 40-for-1 consolidation of both classes of ordinary shares, with fractional entitlements rounded up, in an extraordinary general meeting that drew about 90.86% of eligible voting power. Investors also backed a capital reorganization that first reduces the par value of authorized shares and then enlarges authorized capital to 500 million ordinary shares, reallocating the reduction in issued capital to the share premium account. Together, these measures significantly reshape Megan Holdings’ capital base and decision-making procedures, giving the company more flexibility to issue equity and act swiftly on routine shareholder matters. The pending implementation of the share consolidation in the Nasdaq marketplace will be announced in a subsequent regulatory filing and will mark the operational transition of the new capital structure for market participants.

Megan Holdings Limited is a Cayman Islands-incorporated company headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and listed on The Nasdaq Capital Market in the U.S. It operates as a foreign private issuer, with a dual-class ordinary share structure comprising Class A and Class B shares, and is subject to U.S. securities regulation under Form 20-F reporting requirements.

The company’s governance framework includes the use of extraordinary general meetings to obtain shareholder approval for significant corporate actions, such as share consolidations, capital reorganizations and amendments to its memorandum and articles of association. Its sizeable shareholder base and high voting participation indicate an engaged investor group for key structural decisions.

On August 21, 2026, Megan Holdings Limited shareholders approved a 40-for-1 consolidation of both Class A and Class B ordinary shares, with fractional entitlements rounded up, in an extraordinary general meeting that achieved a quorum representing about 90.86% of voting power. The move aims to restructure the share capital while potentially supporting compliance with Nasdaq listing requirements and improving the perceived value and trading profile of the stock.

Shareholders also passed a capital reorganization that reduces the par value of authorized shares and then expands authorized capital to 500 million ordinary shares, reallocating the reduction in issued share capital to the share premium account, thereby giving the company greater flexibility for future equity issuance. In tandem, investors approved a new set of amended and restated memorandum and articles of association that embed these changes and lower the threshold for passing ordinary resolutions by written consent from unanimity to a simple majority.

The corporate resolutions collectively streamline Megan Holdings’ capital structure and governance, which may simplify future corporate actions and facilitate faster decision-making on ordinary matters.
